description: Quick-pick fields for the viewer: the five official test targets from docs/CHALLENGE.md. Positions are propagated to epoch 2026.0 so fast movers sit near the field centre in SPHEREx data. Use this list to warm the Live API cache (T05) so the cache ids match what the viewer requests.

provenance.service: SIMBAD TAP, mirror https://simbad.harvard.edu/simbad/sim-tap/sync (simbad.cds.unistra.fr answered 'page unavailable' at the time)
provenance.query: SELECT i.id AS query_id, b.main_id, b.ra, b.dec, b.pmra, b.pmdec, b.coo_bibcode, b.otype FROM basic AS b JOIN ident AS i ON b.oid = i.oidref WHERE i.id IN ('NAME Barnard''s Star', '* eps Ind B', 'WISE J085510.83-071442.5', 'V* RW Aur', 'V* R Dra')

method: ICRS J2000 position plus SIMBAD proper motion (pmra includes cos dec), propagated linearly to epoch 2026.0 and rounded to 1e-4 deg (the Live API cache grid). Parallax and radial velocity ignored (below 1 arcsec for these objects).

fields.name: Barnard's Star
fields.kind: Red dwarf with the largest proper motion of any star

fields.name: Epsilon Indi B
fields.kind: Pair of brown dwarfs orbiting the star Epsilon Indi

fields.name: WISE 0855-0714
fields.note: The challenge text gives RA 08h55m10.831s, Dec -7d14m42.53s, which is the position around 2010 (WISE epoch), about 2 arcmin from the 2026 position used here.
